claims.claim: Reviewers consistently state that the main story is very short compared to the first game.

citations.review_text:
The game is ok. It's literally the exact same game as Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered, with a coat of snow on the map and a different main character that plays almost exactly the same as the other one.
Mechanics and content have been refined from the previous game without really changing much, but at least the puzzles for 2 years-old are gone and there's only 2 currencies now, and things are less repetitive. I particularly enjoyed the side missions with the phone app.
The story is solid and the acting performances are still very good, but, as a lot of other reviewers have said, it's very short (it took me 18 hours to 100% the game and get all achievements, including replaying it with New Game+). I have nothing against shorter stories, the first one was too long for my taste, but the game comes almost at the same price as Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered and Marvel's Spider-Man 2, that's way too much given how much smaller in scope everything is!

I don't know how long the developers had to make it, but you can tell they recycled as much as they could, including animations.
There's way less unlockables, way less gadgets, way less suits (and they are really not looking great to me compared to the previous game), way less enemy variety, basically only 2 bosses, and the suits power are very minor buffs compared to the various choices of powerful abilities that was given previously.

There's no way I can give a no recommendation to this, because it's still very enjoyable, but I just want to say that for the asking price this is a hard sell. However, if you get it for around 20€ on sales like I did, then it's a good price to pay for what you get. Just don't pay full price for it!

Oh boy where do I start with this mess?

This game at best is a $20 DLC for a xbox360 era game, masquerading as a full price AAA game. Very embarrassing to think this was a PS5 launch title and no wonder that console struggled. 

A few things I liked:

- New Venom powers are kinda cool for Miles, but not super crazy
- The prowler was an interesting character in the story
- Camo ability is also a cool addition for Miles

But thats it honestly, here are the major flaws:

- Story is incredibly short (finished main story and 85% of whole game in less than 10 hours)
- Boss battles that were a huge element of the first game with the iconic Spider-Main villains largely absent from this game with the exception of Rhino for all of what felt like 5 minutes, no real attempt to make unique villains for Miles apart from the tinkerer which was a bit lackluster given it was the final boss battle and compared to the 2018 version's final boss battle very unfulfilling
- This is a big one, very forced woke nonsense throughout the whole game and story. Miles mom is a Latina politician, there's deaf girl who constantly shows up for whatever reason, a lesbian couple runs a homeless shelter. Seems like the budget for this game went to the woke propaganda over the actual game-play and content

Verdict:

Not worth full price, honestly wouldn't buy for more than $10. Get on a sale. Sony and Insomniac are huge studios with massive budgets. Making a black Spider-Main in Harlem is great, but if you put half the effort that was made towards all the needless woke nonsense instead towards good villains, unique story and exciting game play, maybe you would've actually managed to make a good game.

I did enjoy the 2018 version, so this series is 1-2 so far. I'll try Spider-Man 2 and see how that is

An Amazing Winter Web-Slinging Experience (If you can catch it on sale!)

Miles was set up perfectly in Spider-Man Remastered, and this game does a fantastic job expanding on his character and diving deeper into his past. Setting the game in wintertime Harlem was an incredible choice—it gives the city a completely different, refreshing vibe compared to the first game. The Christmas lights and winter ambiance look amazing. Honestly, I almost wish I had played this during the winter instead of the summer just to match the atmosphere! As for the villains, the game handles them great. Without giving too much away, I'll just say it really is a small world!

While Peter definitely has the edge when it comes to the sheer number of gadgets, Miles' unique abilities are awesome. The addition of Venom blasts and camouflage completely changes the combat flow, allowing you to play much more aggressively than you could with Peter. It makes stepping into Miles' shoes feel fresh and distinct, making the expansion entirely worthwhile.

The PC port is fantastic. The game ran smoothly for me with zero lag, even on the highest settings. The winter environments really shine and perform flawlessly.

If you're a fan of Spider-Man games or the character in general, I highly recommend this. However, the main storyline is noticeably shorter than Spiderman Remastered. Because of the shorter runtime, I definitely recommend picking this up when it goes on sale.

- Upgrades were boring and not as rewarding as Spider-Man
- It's the same map and feels a tad too spread out
- Aaron and Jeff's mixtape was hot ass

Oh boy where do I start with this mess?

This game at best is a $20 DLC for a xbox360 era game, masquerading as a full price AAA game. Very embarrassing to think this was a PS5 launch title and no wonder that console struggled. 

A few things I liked:

- New Venom powers are kinda cool for Miles, but not super crazy
- The prowler was an interesting character in the story
- Camo ability is also a cool addition for Miles

But thats it honestly, here are the major flaws:

- Story is incredibly short (finished main story and 85% of whole game in less than 10 hours)
- Boss battles that were a huge element of the first game with the iconic Spider-Main villains largely absent from this game with the exception of Rhino for all of what felt like 5 minutes, no real attempt to make unique villains for Miles apart from the tinkerer which was a bit lackluster given it was the final boss battle and compared to the 2018 version's final boss battle very unfulfilling
- This is a big one, very forced woke nonsense throughout the whole game and story. Miles mom is a Latina politician, there's deaf girl who constantly shows up for whatever reason, a lesbian couple runs a homeless shelter. Seems like the budget for this game went to the woke propaganda over the actual game-play and content

Verdict:

Not worth full price, honestly wouldn't buy for more than $10. Get on a sale. Sony and Insomniac are huge studios with massive budgets. Making a black Spider-Main in Harlem is great, but if you put half the effort that was made towards all the needless woke nonsense instead towards good villains, unique story and exciting game play, maybe you would've actually managed to make a good game.

I did enjoy the 2018 version, so this series is 1-2 so far. I'll try Spider-Man 2 and see how that is

Similar to my last review of Spider-Man Remastered, this game felt more like a continuation than a full-fledged sequel—closer to DLC in scope.

Because of that, I wouldn't recommend paying the full $49.99 price. I'd definitely wait for a sale. I picked it up for $19.99, and at that price, I think it's absolutely worth it.

Overall, I’m giving it a 9/10, the same score I gave the previous installment. The graphics look great, and the gameplay is very similar, with a few improvements—especially some new finishers that I personally really enjoyed!

If you’re interested, give it a shot when it goes on sale. At a discounted price, you won’t regret it!

[h1]Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales. Small Game, Huge Personality[/h1]

⭐ [b]Rating: 8/10[/b]
🕒 [b]Playtime: 20+ Hours[/b]

[i]It may be shorter than Spider-Man Remastered, but it absolutely doesn't feel like a DLC.[/i]

[hr]

[h2]🕷️ Traversal, Combat & Animation[/h2]

From a [b]Game Design perspective[/b], Miles Morales builds on the foundation of Spider-Man Remastered while giving Miles his own identity.

The traversal feels incredibly fluid, and the new Venom abilities, finishers, and animations make combat feel different rather than simply recycled. The animation blending and movement flow are still some of the strongest parts of the game.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3780611928

[hr]

[h2]🌆 Art Direction & Level Design[/h2]

The art direction is beautiful. Manhattan looks incredible, especially with the winter atmosphere, lighting, reflections, and environmental details.

The level design and environments show a lot of care, and the city feels designed around Miles rather than simply reused from the previous game.

And of course...

[b]The Cat. 🐈‍⬛[/b]

One of my absolute favorite parts of the game.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3779882194

[hr]

[h2]🎵 Music & Story[/h2]

The soundtrack is honestly next level. The hip-hop inspired tracks fit Miles perfectly and make the world feel much more personal to him.

The story is also very well written. Insomniac once again understands how to make its characters feel human, while keeping the superhero spectacle intact.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3780542816

[hr]

[h2]⚙️ Optimization & Technical Issues[/h2]

Performance is generally excellent. I played at [b]1440p Native[/b] on an RTX 4070 and the game ran very well.

However, the game can be surprisingly CPU-intensive with Ray Tracing enabled. My Ryzen 7 7700X occasionally became the bottleneck, causing lower GPU utilization. After optimi…

Pretty dang good "Sequel" to Spider-Man. I only give it the quotations because it definitely feels like an extended DLC that kinda ballooned into a full blown game. It is significantly shorter than the first game so I do think that the 50$ standard price is maybe a smidge too high IMO but getting it on sale was well worth it. 100% took about 25 hours, 21~ hours for the first playthrough then the rest was NG+ which is unfortunately required to 100%. I loved all the cool different suits you can unlock and the side stories/missions were pretty fun too! As expected the traversal around the city and during combat are the primary highlights for the game and that alone was enjoyable enough even if you may dislike the other parts of the game.

8/10
But not as great as 
Insomniacs first game to be honest, I had fun with what the game offered and I loved how different Miles was from Peter by how they swing and fight.... But I really think this game should of been a $20-30 DLC included Spiderman1 over a whole new game itself, story was far too short for my liking but that's about It the game was fun can't wait to try Spiderman 2

A great game, only that it is very short, you just connect with the story and that's the end. This is more like a bigger expansion of Spider Man 2018 and it's very good. I ran into a lot of bugs that haven't been fixed yet, I don't know why.


Swinging in snowy New York is beautiful and gives a unique experience. The gameplay is familiar, but it is different and much more interesting than Peter's. It is much improved because Miles unique bio-electric Venom abilities and camouflage powers. These additions make encounters feel fresh and provide more options during battles.


If you enjoyed the first Spider-Man game, this is an easy recommendation. It may not be as big, but it has its own identity and delivers a really fun Spider-Man experience.

citations.review_text: The best game from the Insomniac sage for sure, 9/10. It’s my favorite story of the three games so far by a lot, Miles being the lone spider while Peter is away is such a fun concept for spider man. Miles as the focus is really awesome and I loved playing the segments where he’s not suited and we get to learn about his personal life, way better than the horrid MJ missions. I really enjoy playing as Miles a lot more than Peter, his stealth invis capabilities make stealth way cooler which is where I find a lot of the fun in the game, he also has his signature lighting abilities that are super fun to use in combat. The vibe of New York in winter is so awesome, I love swinging through the snowy streets with all the lights up it is so relaxing to throw on a nice playlist and light one up while you swing around. It does have less content than the other two games out but it is also cheaper making it totally worth the price. So far the best spider man game

Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales builds upon its predecessor in a lot of ways, including new combat mechanics and a New York City that feels even more lived-in this time around, with holiday lights decorating the streets that are just as fun as before to web-swing through. But the biggest improvement I noticed is the performance of the PC port itself. No more random crashes when the game wants to load some big setpiece into the city (like Shocker's wave of destruction or Sable's checkpoints) before you start the mission properly, which was a major game-breaking issue in the first game that forced me to load my save and play on a different PC just to get past those sections that would otherwise prevent me entirely from playing. In this charming sequel, those issues are gone and the game runs flawlessly on my preferred PC. My least favorite part was probably the music sampling sidequest, which says a lot about how good this game is because that side content is at least conceptually very cool and unpacks interesting lore about Miles' family's past. Overall, if you enjoyed the first Marvel's Spider-Man, don't skip out on this "Spider-Man 1.5" before playing Spider-Man 2. It's absolutely worth your time.

This game was a lot better than I though it was going to be.

It plays very similarly to the Amazing Spider-Man remastered, which is to say that the gameplay is fantastic. 

The traversal and combat are thrilling and the combat is pretty darn good. The combat relies a little too heavily on venom powers, which takes away a little of the acrobatic awesomeness of the first one, but it all works, I enjoyed every minute of it.

The city is just as great as it was in the Amazing Spider-Man remaster, although it feels a little smaller, but not in a way that serves to be overly limiting. There is a small section of the city in the Harlem District as street level that is exceptionally peak. It looks like it was pulled right out of the comics. It's an idealized version of Harlem with lots of street art and cool structures. The people are all dressed in colorful cloths and have interesting animation and walla, and the level of detail from the fur on the hoodies to the signs in the store windows is just out of this world. The game doesn't really give you much reason to explore that area at the ground level, but it is worth checking out, especially if you like Miles in the comics. It is done well! It is cooler than anything in the city from the first game.

The story isn't bad. It does feel a little rushed, but it manages to stay coherent and compelling from start to finish. The depiction of Miles himself is a little off, he is portrayed in a manner that seems very simpy and vulnerable in a way that is not overpowering, but does contrast poorly with the steadfast nature of his character in the comics. The supporting cast however is outstanding and portrayed in a way that is extremely faithful to the comics and very entertaining. Miles is the main character in the game without question, but by the time you are done you will be very familiar with all the people in his life, they aren't bit parts in the story they are very much a part of it.

First of all, this is probably the worst optimized game i've ever played. my specs are more than enough for what they reccomended and yet even on mid setting i still had lag and even pauses throughout so much of my gameplay to load the map right in front of me. Multiple times ive actually clipped into a building that wasnt fully loaded only to get trapped inside because it loaded after i fell in. on top of this there were a handful of bugs throughout the entire game and its just very disappointing considering how big the studio is. I got it on sale for about 20 bucks and id still say it wasnt worth it. However on the bright side the combat was very fun and the movement felt great whenever there werent pauses. The story was decent at best, it kept me interested even though a lot of the twists were predictable and boring/generic. But on replay in new game+ i found out only a handful of cutscenes can even be skipped for some reason so youll have to sit through 80% of the cutscenes a second time if you wanna finish new game+. A big issue i had with the core gameplay is how it feels so forced to do stealth because if you dont youll get attacked by too many enemies and die, but the stealth is so boring that it just isnt fun at all and it makes you wish you were actually fighting them. Lastly, all of the variety in collectibles and side content throughout the map makes it very enjoyable to run around getting every last collectible as long as you dont run into many performance issues going from place to place. With a lower price point and a more polished experience this game might be worth it for the 25-ish hours of content.

I personally would not recommend this game to many people. I always consider price, and this game was not worth it. I also used the first Spider-Man game as a base because it comes before this game. It is ten dollars cheaper, I absolutely love the camouflage mechanic, and the story is kinda alright. That is where the positives end. For starters, one small problem is that a good amount of the cutscenes are not skippable. I don't think it's that bad, but when I have to do a 3rd playthrough, I want to skip these cutscenes. The story also isn't as interesting as the first game. I understand that it's hard to do much because Miles Morales is a new Spider-Man, but I just wish they could make a more intriguing story. The Spider-Man app with the missions is decently fun, but the other side missions are kinda boring or just way harder than they should be. In Spider-Man, the Taskmaster and Screwball challenges were either delightfully hard or somewhat easy but still have some difficulty. These Peter challenges leave zero room for mistakes and force you to work on only one action. I hate this because it forces me to limit the ways I can take out enemies. The time capsules are boring. They require as much as the backpacks, or maybe a little more. I'm not a fan of the warehouse missions because, unlike Spider-Man, we only get one wave and can easily be beaten if you just go invis. Of course you can fight with your bare hands, but there's no incentive to because those warehouses don't have their own currency, making you want to perfect them. There's also just the lack of currencies. Spider-Man rewards you for finding backpacks and locations, completing bases well, and committing crimes perfectly. This is not reflected in Miles Morales because most unique side quests give the same currency. The story also had a major flaw. Whenever it seems Miles might die, he's given a new ability.
